chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sindi ibn Muhammad from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He gave a ruling regarding a man who married a slave woman, then found means (i.e., financial ability), and did not desire to divorce the slave woman; he was asked about her. He ruled: 'A free woman may be married to a slave woman, but a slave woman may not be married to a free woman if the free woman was the first of the two with him. And if the slave woman was with him before the marriage of the free woman to the slave woman, he shall divide for the free woman two-thirds of his wealth and his self (i.e., his time/attention), meaning his maintenance, and for the slave woman one-third of his wealth and his self.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on dividing wealth and time between a free wife and a slave wife when the husband gains wealth?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential hierarchy in polygyny, establishing that a free woman can be married to a slave woman, but not vice versa, while detailing the equitable division of wealth and time (maintenance/attention) between the two wives based on the order of their marriage. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on justice and the specific rights of slave women within the family structure, ensuring their financial and emotional entitlements are preserved even when the husband gains means. The hadith underscores the principle that the status of the first wife determines the structural arrangement of subsequent marriages, highlighting the nuanced application of Quranic principles of fairness in marital relations.
